title: A Shonen rewriting of David and Goliath: Baki vs Hanayama in Grappler Baki
summary: A Manga Motivation essay reading the Baki vs Hanayama fight in Grappler Baki as a shonen retelling of David versus Goliath. NH analyses size versus speed and technique, the flow of power, youth and innocence, stubbornness, and how spirit rather than physique decided the bout.
claims: The David vs Goliath story symbolises surpassing the physical limits imposed at birth and the undying force of hope
Shonen needs underdog heroes so characters can start low and rise; Baki is 5'2" and 180 lb against Hanayama at 6'3" and 365 lb
Hanayama represents genetic injustice: born with size and strength, whereas Baki earned his through thousands of hours of training
Fighting someone twice your size up close is a terrible idea, which is why weight classes exist
Giants are slower to rotate and strike, so speed and technique can beat them, but you need the guts to get within grabbing range
You cannot teach size; one clean blow from a much larger fighter can erase all of a smaller fighter's advantages
When clever tactics stop being enough you must be willing to put your body on the line
Stubbornness can be frightfully effective: if you never give up you cannot lose
What dictated the fight was spirit, not physical differences: the one who always found the strength to stand up triumphed
In Grappler Baki violent conflict naturally ends in peaceful resolution and fighting is a form of social interaction
